vocabulary.meaning_en: the area of a town around where you live
vocabulary.example: There are many shops in our neighborhood.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a green public area with trees and grass
vocabulary.example: We have a picnic in the park every Friday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a quiet building with books you can read or borrow
vocabulary.note_ar: لا تخلطها مع bookshop = محل بيع الكتب
vocabulary.example: I borrowed two novels from the library.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a place where children go to learn
vocabulary.example: My school is next to the park.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a shop that makes and sells bread and cakes
vocabulary.example: The bakery smells wonderful in the morning.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a shop where you buy medicine
vocabulary.note_ar: ph تُنطق f، وفي بريطانيا يُقال أيضاً chemist's
vocabulary.example: Is there a pharmacy open at night?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a place where you buy stamps and send letters and parcels
vocabulary.example: I need to send this parcel from the post office.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small place to drink coffee and eat light food
vocabulary.example: Let's meet at the café on the corner.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a building where you watch films
vocabulary.example: There's a new film at the cinema.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the building where the police work
vocabulary.example: He reported the lost wallet at the police station.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a building where sick or injured people are treated
vocabulary.example: She works as a nurse at the hospital.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a place on the street where you wait for the bus
vocabulary.example: I waited at the bus stop for twenty minutes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who lives next door or near you
vocabulary.example: Our neighbor helped us carry the boxes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who owns or runs a small shop
vocabulary.example: The shopkeeper gave me a free sweet.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who delivers letters to homes
vocabulary.example: The mailman comes every morning at nine.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a member of the police
vocabulary.example: A police officer helped the old man cross the road.

vocabulary.meaning_en: putting a lot of effort into your work
vocabulary.example: She is a hard-working student.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an outdoor area with slides and swings for children
vocabulary.example: The kids are on the swings in the playground.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an open public area in a town where people gather
vocabulary.example: There's a market in the main square on Sundays.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a public building where neighbors meet for events and classes
vocabulary.example: They teach English at the community center.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a large grassy area for playing sports
vocabulary.example: We play football on the sports field after school.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to go to see a place or a person
vocabulary.example: We visit my grandparents every weekend.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to take something from someone and give it back later
vocabulary.example: Can I borrow your pen?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to come together in one place
vocabulary.example: People gathered in the square to watch the show.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a wide main street, often with trees on both sides
vocabulary.example: The museum is on Fifth Avenue.

vocabulary.meaning_en: white lines on the road where people can cross safely
vocabulary.example: Always cross the road at the crosswalk.

vocabulary.meaning_en: red, yellow and green lights that control traffic
vocabulary.example: Turn left at the next traffic light.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long seat for several people, often in a park
vocabulary.example: They sat on a bench and fed the birds.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to travel around a place to learn about it
vocabulary.example: We spent the day exploring the old city.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a paper cover you put a letter in
vocabulary.example: Write the address on the envelope.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to speak very quietly
vocabulary.example: She whispered the answer in my ear.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in a worried or anxious way
vocabulary.example: He looked nervously at the clock.

vocabulary.meaning_en: strange and difficult to explain
vocabulary.example: We got a mysterious phone call last night.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to smile widely
vocabulary.example: He grinned when he saw the cake.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to breathe in suddenly because you are surprised or shocked
vocabulary.example: She gasped when she saw the price.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a collection of gold, money or valuable things
vocabulary.example: The pirates hid their treasure on an island.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something used to catch someone or a dangerous trick
vocabulary.example: Be careful, it could be a trap.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an exciting and unusual experience
vocabulary.example: Our trip to the desert was a real adventure.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small paper you stick on a letter to pay for sending it
vocabulary.example: I need a stamp for this letter.

fine_lines.title: street vs avenue
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان بمعنى شارع، والفرق في الحجم والتخطيط. street شارع عادي صغير أو متوسط عليه بيوت ومحلات. avenue شارع رئيسي عريض جداً، غالباً مزيّن بالأشجار على الجانبين في المدن الكبيرة، وتتفرع منه الشوارع الأصغر.

examples.sentence: I live on a quiet street near the school.
There's a small bakery on our street.
The parade went down the main avenue.
Tall trees line both sides of the avenue.

fine_lines.title: sidewalk vs crosswalk
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان للمشاة. sidewalk هو الرصيف الجانبي الذي يمشي عليه الناس بأمان على جانبي الطريق. crosswalk هو ممر المشاة: الخطوط البيضاء المرسومة في وسط الشارع التي تعبر من خلالها إلى الجهة الأخرى.

examples.sentence: Kids should ride their bikes on the sidewalk.
Cars must stop for people at the crosswalk.

fine_lines.title: walk down vs walk up (the street)
fine_lines.explanation_ar: لا نقول عادة walk in the street، بل walk down the street أو walk up the street. في الكلام اليومي الاثنان بنفس المعنى، و down هي الأشيع. نظرياً down نحو وسط المدينة و up خارجها، أما عملياً فالفرق يظهر فقط إذا كان الشارع منحدراً فعلاً (نازل = down، طالع = up).

examples.sentence: We walked down the street to the café.
It's hard to walk up this steep hill.

fine_lines.title: library vs bookshop
fine_lines.explanation_ar: library مكتبة عامة تقرأ فيها الكتب أو تستعيرها ثم تعيدها مجاناً. bookshop (أو bookstore) محل تشتري منه الكتب.

examples.sentence: I borrowed this book from the library.
I bought a new dictionary at the bookshop.

expressions.example: After walking down the avenue for two hours, Ali ran out of steam and sat on a bench.

expressions.meaning_ar: يواجه موقفاً صعباً أو مؤلماً بشجاعة ويتحمّله
expressions.example: I hate the dentist, but I bit the bullet and made an appointment.
You won't believe this — I won the prize!

expressions.meaning_ar: يتحقق من الأمر / يذهب ليرى بنفسه
expressions.example: There's a new café downtown. Let's check it out.

expressions.meaning_ar: غنيّ عن القول / واضح دون أن يُقال
expressions.example: It goes without saying that you should be on time.

grammar.title: Past perfect continuous: the cause of a past result
grammar.explanation_ar: الماضي التام المستمر (had been + فعل ing) نستخدمه لنشرح سبب نتيجة رأيناها في الماضي: نشاط استمر فترة قبلها. النتيجة نضعها في الماضي البسيط، والسبب المستمر في الماضي التام المستمر. had been ثابتة مع كل الضمائر.
examples: He was very tired. He had been playing football for two hours.
The street was wet because it had been raining all night.
The children were dirty because they had been playing in the playground.

grammar.title: Past continuous for background actions
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم الماضي المستمر (was/were + ing) لوصف حدث كان مستمراً في خلفية القصة. وإذا جاء فعلان مستمران لنفس الفاعل فلا نكرر was.
examples: Emma was sitting on a bench, sharing a bag of sweets.
They were talking and laughing in the square.

grammar.title: should + base verb for advice
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم should (ينبغي أن) لتقديم نصيحة أو اقتراح، ويأتي بعدها الفعل في المصدر بدون to.
examples: We should take this to the police station.
You should visit the new library.

questions.question: You can borrow books for free from the ___.
The white lines on the road where people cross are called the:
A wide main street with trees on both sides is an:
The street was wet because it ___ all night.
questions.explanation_ar: سبب مستمر لنتيجة في الماضي = الماضي التام المستمر.

questions.question: The children were dirty because they ___ in the playground.
questions.explanation_ar: ربط سبب مستمر بنتيجة في الماضي = had been playing.

questions.question: We ___ take this letter to the police station.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد should يأتي الفعل في المصدر بدون to.

questions.question: "After two hours of shopping, I ran out of steam." This means:
questions.explanation_ar: run out of steam = فقد طاقته فجأة.

questions.question: "I'm scared of the exam, but I'll bite the bullet." This means:
questions.explanation_ar: bite the bullet = يواجه الموقف الصعب بشجاعة.

questions.question: Choose the most natural sentence:
choices: We walked in the street to the café.
We walked down the street to the café.
We walked on down street to the café.
We walked at the street to the café.
questions.explanation_ar: التعبير الطبيعي walk down the street.
